title: Life on the Prairie
description: Explore North American grassland through its grasses, large grazers, and burrowing animals.
cardDescription: Explore North American grassland through its grasses, large grazers, and burrowing animals.
focus: A prairie is a grassland ecosystem, not simply an empty field. The clues describe the plants, animals, and ground features that make up the habitat.
solvingTip: Use the clue’s category: grazing animal, burrow, plant, or open landscape.
words: Large grazing mammal often called buffalo in North America
Underground passage or home dug by a grassland animal
Burrowing rodent associated with underground tunnels
Group of large grazing mammals such as bison
Narrow-leaved plant covering much of a prairie
Below-ground plant part extending into prairie soil
Reproductive structure eaten by many grassland birds
Bird of prey seen hunting above open country
Stocky digging mammal with strong claws
Wide relatively level area of open land
Moving air sweeping across an open grassland

answerNotes.PRAIRIE: Prairies include diverse plant and animal communities; they are not all identical in rainfall, soil, or vegetation height.
answerNotes.BISON: American bison are distinct from the true buffalo species of Africa and Asia.
answerNotes.BURROW: A burrow is the structure, while the animal occupying it may be a rodent or another kind of creature.
answerNotes.GOPHER: Gopher names an animal group, not every small mammal living under a lawn or prairie.
answerNotes.HERD: Herd names the group rather than the grassland habitat it occupies.

title: Desert Animals After Sunset
description: Picture familiar desert animals through their ears, tails, paws, and the cooling evening scene.
cardDescription: Picture familiar desert animals through their ears, tails, paws, and the cooling evening scene.
focus: These clues identify visible animals and ordinary surroundings without specialist animal-group names.
solvingTip: Try a short body part or evening word first.
words: Pointed-eared animal related to a dog
Bird of prey often heard after desert sunset
Flying mammal active around the desert at dusk
Small reptile with a long tail in many desert habitats
Long-eared animal related to a rabbit
Loose grains underfoot on some desert ground
Hard natural object providing a sheltered spot
Desert plant often covered with spines
Dark period after the desert sun has set
Fading evening light before full darkness
Rear body part of the fox or lizard
Body part helping the animal hear
Body part used to see in the evening light

answerNotes.FOX: Desert foxes include several kinds adapted to dry surroundings.
answerNotes.OWL: Owls have feathers and wings, unlike the nearby flying mammal.
answerNotes.BAT: A bat is a mammal rather than a bird.
answerNotes.LIZARD: Lizards differ from snakes in usually having visible legs.
answerNotes.HARE: Hares and rabbits are related but are not identical groups.

title: Birds in a Florida Marsh
description: Watch familiar wading birds through their legs, wings, bills, and watery surroundings.
cardDescription: Watch familiar wading birds through their legs, wings, bills, and watery surroundings.
focus: Long legs help these birds stand in shallow water while they look for food.
solvingTip: Short body-part and color words help cross the bird names.

Usually white wading bird related to herons

answerNotes.HERON: Herons often look for food while standing or moving through shallow water.
answerNotes.EGRET: Egret is a familiar name for several heron relatives, not one single species.
answerNotes.MARSH: A marsh has wet ground and water-loving vegetation.
answerNotes.BILL: Bill is the everyday bird term used here rather than a payment request.
answerNotes.WING: The wings carry the bird through the air rather than supporting it while standing.

title: An Alpine Meadow in Summer
description: Visit a high mountain meadow through its short growing season, low plants, and familiar wildlife.
cardDescription: Visit a high mountain meadow through its short growing season, low plants, and familiar wildlife.
focus: Alpine habitats lie above the tree line. Low growth and a short summer distinguish them from wooded slopes farther down the mountain.
solvingTip: Use the elevation or body feature named by the clue, then try the short landscape words.
words: Describing the high mountain zone above the tree line
Large ground-dwelling squirrel found in many mountain regions
Small rabbit relative living among mountain rocks
Accumulation of broken rock on a mountain slope
Upper elevation boundary of tree growth, with spaces omitted
Open area covered mainly by grasses and other low plants
Low nonflowering plant growing in moist mountain patches
Long narrow crest of a mountain
Frozen precipitation lingering in high shaded places
Open mountain flower during the short growing season
Hard material forming the meadow's surrounding outcrops
Narrow-leaved plant in the mountain meadow
Moving air passing over exposed high ground
Plant anchor beneath a shallow mountain soil

answerNotes.ALPINE: Alpine describes elevation and habitat; it is not limited to the European Alps.
answerNotes.MARMOT: Marmots are rodents in the squirrel family, often associated with open rocky or meadow habitat.
answerNotes.PIKA: A pika belongs to the rabbit-and-hare order rather than the rodent group.
answerNotes.TALUS: Talus describes loose rock debris, a setting where animals such as pikas may shelter.
answerNotes.TREELINE: Tree line depends on climate and local conditions rather than one worldwide elevation.

title: Animals of the Northern Tundra
description: Explore a cold northern landscape through low vegetation and the animals adapted to its seasons.
cardDescription: Explore a cold northern landscape through low vegetation and the animals adapted to its seasons.
focus: Tundra supports low-growing vegetation where conditions limit tree growth. The clues distinguish mammal features, bird plumage, and the seasonal background around them.
solvingTip: Use a distinctive covering or body part to separate the animal names from habitat words.
words: Cold treeless region supporting low vegetation
North American name for a wild reindeer
Northern grouse whose plumage commonly changes toward white in winter
Shaggy northern hoofed mammal with a thick insulating undercoat
Partnership of a fungus with an alga or cyanobacterium
Branched head structure shed and regrown by deer species
Hard foot covering on a caribou
Small nonflowering plant in many damp tundra areas
White frozen precipitation covering the winter ground
Sheltered resting or breeding place of a northern fox
Insulating hair covering a northern mammal

answerNotes.TUNDRA: Tundra occurs in northern and high mountain settings; treeless does not mean entirely without plants.
answerNotes.CARIBOU: Caribou and reindeer belong to the same species, though the names reflect different regional and domestic contexts.
answerNotes.PTARMIGAN: Ptarmigan are birds; seasonal feather changes vary with species, sex, and conditions.
answerNotes.MUSKOX: Muskoxen are related to the goat-and-sheep group rather than being domestic cattle.
answerNotes.LICHEN: A lichen is a biological partnership, not a moss despite some similar-looking low growth forms.
